Nothing too complicated, I'm not super tech-savvy, just needs to be clear and easy to read at a glance.

query_text:
Okay so I'm trying to build an internal portal for our research sites to submit regulatory documents, and I need help designing the actual UI for it — both the submission side (what the sites see) and the internal review side (what my team sees). It's a bit complicated so let me try to explain all of it.

**The site-facing submission flow:**

When a study site logs in, they should land on a dashboard that shows them exactly which documents we're expecting from them — like a checklist. Think things like: Investigator CV, Lab Certificate, IRB Approval Letter, Consent Form (latest version), Financial Disclosure Form, etc. Each document type should have a little label showing whether it's still missing, pending review, rejected, or approved. A green checkmark when it's done, something red or orange if it was rejected, and a clock icon or something for "under review." Sites need to be able to see at a glance what's still outstanding.

When they actually go to upload — and this part is really important to me — the form needs to validate the file before it even finishes uploading. Like if we say we need a PDF and they try to drag in an Excel file or a .docx, it should immediately say "wrong file type, we need PDF only" and not let them proceed. Same thing for file size — we probably want a 25MB limit per file. Each document type in our system has its own rules (some allow PDF only, some might allow PDF or JPEG for like a scanned certificate), so the validation has to be per document slot, not a blanket rule.

There should be a visible progress bar for each file as it's uploading — like I need the site coordinators to actually see it moving, not just a spinning wheel. And if something fails mid-upload, they should get a clear message that says to try again, not just a generic error.

After they've uploaded everything for a given submission packet — let's say it's an "Initial Site Regulatory Binder" — there should be a final review step where they can see all the files they've attached, confirm the site name and protocol number are correct, and then hit submit. That step should feel like a checkpoint, not just a button.

**Rejection and re-upload:**

If my team rejects a file, the site needs to get a notification (in-portal is fine, email is bonus) that says specifically which document was rejected and WHY. Like "Investigator CV rejected — document is expired, please upload a CV dated within the last 2 years." Not just "rejected." Then there should be a clear button right on their dashboard to re-upload just that one document without having to redo the whole submission.

**The internal review side:**

My team's view should show all submissions across all sites in a table or list — site name, protocol, submission date, status (complete/incomplete/under review/approved), and how many documents are still pending review. We should be able to click into a submission and see each document listed out, preview or download it individually, and then mark it as approved or rejected with a required reason field for rejections.

Once a full submission is approved, there should be a button to download the whole thing as a ZIP file, organized by document type. Sponsors sometimes ask us for everything at once and right now I'm manually zipping folders which is a nightmare.

**Audit trail:**

Every single upload, download, approval, and rejection needs to be logged somewhere visible — who did it, what file, what time. My team needs to be able to pull this up if a sponsor ever questions whether we received something. It doesn't have to be fancy, just a sortable log table on each submission's detail page, and maybe a separate export option.

Design-wise, it should feel clean and professional — this is a regulated industry so nothing too playful, but it also shouldn't look like it was built in 2005. Clear typography, status colors that are obvious (green/red/yellow), and it should work fine on a laptop browser. Mobile isn't a priority for us.

Can you build this out? I know it's a lot — feel free to start with the site-facing multi-step upload form and the submission checklist dashboard, and we can layer in the internal review UI after.

ok so I'm building out the admin/management backend for my diet logging app and I need a pretty comprehensive dashboard for managing food entries — specifically focused on calorie counts and glycemic index (GI) data. let me just dump everything I need here:

**main data table** — I need a full-featured table listing all logged food items. each row should show: food name, category (like grains, fruits, protein, dairy, etc.), calories per 100g, GI value, GI classification (low/medium/high — color coded please, green/yellow/red), serving size, date added, and status (active / pending review / flagged). the table should support column sorting, and I want sticky headers when scrolling.

**filtering + search** — there needs to be a filter panel on the left or top (I'm fine with either). filters should include: category multiselect, GI range slider (0–100), calorie range input (min/max), status dropdown, and a date range picker for when entries were added. also a search bar that does fuzzy match on food name. importantly — filters should apply in real time or have an explicit "apply" button, not both mixed together, just pick one and be consistent. and when no results match the current filters, show a clear empty state with a reset filters button.

**batch actions** — I need to be able to select multiple rows and do bulk operations: bulk approve (set to active), bulk flag, bulk delete. the bulk action bar should only appear when at least one row is selected. if I try to delete, show a confirmation modal that lists how many items are being deleted and warns me if any of them are currently referenced in users' meal logs.

**inline editing** — for the calorie and GI fields specifically, I want inline editing directly in the table cell. click to edit, show an input field with validation (GI must be 0–100, calories must be positive number), and save on blur or Enter key. if validation fails, show the error inline next to the field, not a toast.

**detail drawer** — clicking a food name should open a side drawer (not a new page) showing the full record: all fields, an edit form, a history log of who changed what and when, and which users have this item in their recent meal logs. the drawer should be closable via ESC or clicking outside.

**stats summary bar** at the top — just some quick numbers: total food items, how many are pending review, how many flagged, and average GI across all active items. these should update when filters are active to reflect filtered set, not always global totals (except maybe a small label saying "filtered" so it's clear).

**edge cases I care about** — loading skeletons while data fetches, error state if the API fails (with a retry button), empty state for first-time use with a CTA to add the first item, and if someone tries to access a food entry that's been deleted by someone else simultaneously, show a gentle notification instead of crashing the view.

design-wise — clean and functional, nothing too flashy. think a neutral palette with clear typography hierarchy. the GI color coding is the main visual signal so don't let anything else compete with it too much.
